title: When is Test-Time Adaptation Identifiable From Unlabeled Evidence?
abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) offers many ways to update a deployed model without labels, but choosing the wrong update can make a strong source model worse. Recent methods therefore try to predict which adaptation will work from unlabeled test data. We ask a prior question: does the evidence given to the selector contain enough information to determine the best action at all? We show that this is not guaranteed, even with a perfect selector. If an observation channel makes two deployments look the same while their TTA rankings differ, reliable selection is impossible from that channel; richer evidence can restore the decision only when it resolves the relevant ambiguity. We make this boundary exact in a finite-batch Gaussian TTA model, where doing nothing beats mean recentering for small shifts, recentering wins beyond a unique critical shift, and the boundary shrinks as $1/\sqrt n$. Public benchmark studies on CIFAR-100-C and DomainNet-126 show the same failure mode with modern TTA methods: changing only deployment structure can reverse the oracle action while global order-blind evidence remains unchanged. The result is a practical way to separate two failure modes that are usually mixed together: a weak selector versus an information channel that cannot support the desired decision in the first place.

title: GHC with stream fusion, used as benchmark in the publication: Higher Order Patterns for Rewrite Rules
abstract: I have added higher order patterns to GHC's rewrite rules which should make stream fusion more viable. So, this dataset contains a development version of the GHC compiler with patches applied to replace the fold/build fusion mechanism with a stream fusion mechanism. I have used this modified version of the GHC compiler to perform the benchmarks in my paper. The benchmarks are performed using Hadrian and on the nofib benchmark suite which is included in the GHC repository.

title: On the Relationship of Unacceptable Arguments to Acceptable Extensions
abstract: In abstract argumentation, admissibility-based semantics occasionally yield counterintuitive results when spurious or self-defeating attacks are present. This has motivated the development of various “weak” semantics, which are united by a common intuition: an argument’s acceptance should be evaluated based on its external stability with respect to other acceptable arguments, rather than all attackers. However, this intuition suffers from vagueness, hence its instantiations vary across the literature. In this paper, we attempt to formalize this intuition into various principles for argumentation semantics. Our analysis of popular semantics in the literature (including stable, preferred, admissible, cogent, and weakly admissible) reveals that few satisfy these criteria simultaneously. To address this gap, we introduce a scheme for relativized semantics which evaluates acceptability only on the sub-framework of credulously acceptable arguments, according to some standard. We further consider fixed points of the operation which returns the sub-framework consisting of all acceptable arguments (according to some semantics); while most classical semantics acquire a fixed point immediately, weak admissibility can require arbitrarily many applications.

title: Enhanced Acoustic Distress Detection and Automated Emergency Alert System
abstract: The work presents a distress detection system based on audio analysis to recognize distress calls and send alerts. It leverages speech-to-text conversion and fuzzy keyword matching to detect distress signals from audio inputs. It works using Assembly AI’s speech recognition API and implements a Flask-based web interface. The performance of the system in the alert dispatch and distress identification is high. In the future, the detection performance and real time streaming capabilities will be further improved. General Terms: Pattern Recognition, Security, Algorithms, Emergency Response, Speech Processing, Audio Analysis, Real-Time Monitoring, Data Handling

title: Robustness of Federated Learning Aggregators under Differential Privacy Noise in Non-IID Scenarios
abstract: Updates in Federated Learning (FL) can leak sensitive data, which is mitigated by record level Differential Privacy (DP) noise; however, this generates a high cost in terms of accuracy, convergence and stability. This study evaluates the impact of different levels of DP noise on FL aggregators: FedAvg, SCAFFOLD, and FedALA. The study considered multi-client scenarios with CIFAR-10 and non-IID datasets. FedALA achieved 80 percent accuracy in two rounds of communication under low noise and 65 percent under high noise, surpassing SCAFFOLD, 20 percent and 11 percent, FedAvg, 19 percent, and lower. Thus, the results indicate that FedALA has the best robustness and privacy-utility trade-off under increasing noise.

title: A quantum reservoir computing approach to quantum stock price forecasting in technology-markets
abstract: We present a quantum reservoir computing (QRC) framework based on a small-scale quantum system comprising at most six interacting qubits, designed for nonlinear financial time-series forecasting. We apply the model to predict future daily closing trading prices of 20 quantum-sector publicly traded companies over the period from April 11, 2020, to April 11, 2025 (exclusive), as well as minute-by-minute trading prices during out-of-market hours on July 7, 2025. Our analysis identifies optimal reservoir parameters that yield stock trend (up/down) classification accuracies exceeding 86%. Importantly, the QRC model is platform-agnostic and can be realized across diverse physical implementations of qubits, including superconducting circuits and trapped ions. These results demonstrate the expressive power and robustness of small-scale quantum reservoirs for modeling complex temporal correlations in financial data, highlighting their potential applicability to real-world forecasting tasks on near-term quantum hardware.

title: What Counts as a Mistake? Annotating Recitation Events in Quran Memorization Transcripts
abstract: Checking Quran recitation from an ASR transcript requires distinguishing unresolved mistakes from repetitions, repairs, opening formulas and accepted spelling differences. We report a completed human annotation of 100 production recording cases: 348 scored units and 162 localized events across ten combined labels. An executable evaluator scores labels and word positions together. A plain diff reaches label-aware F1 0.525 and localization F1 0.826; adapted production cleaner/alignment components reach 0.518 and 0.786, with exact-span F1 0.505 for both. Correcting the adapter's word coordinates recovers all five annotated repetition events, showing why annotation interfaces must be checked before interpreting baseline failures. In a preliminary pilot, eight single 20-minute runs across three coding agents and eight models span label-aware F1 0.143 to 0.892: seven land far above every baseline, and one collapses below the naive diff from a missing normalization step. Across the six, 970 of 972 gold-event instances draw an overlapping prediction, so what remains is not detection but convention: span extent, and the labels whose boundary is stipulated by adjudication rather than visible in the text. Seven of 162 events defeat all six same-day runs, five of them one orthographic rule, and the strongest run still misses the same ones. No run annotated before building, so the pilot measures the algorithm half of the task only.

title: Automatic Lyric Transcription for Greek Songs: Scaling and Task Composition Effects in Whisper Adaptation
abstract: Automatic Lyric Transcription (ALT) remains substantially more challenging than speech recognition due to melodic variability, rhythmic irregularity, and accompaniment interference. This is heightened in low-resource languages like Greek, where no prior benchmark for ALT exists. We present the first controlled study of Whisper adaptation for Greek ALT, investigating model scaling effects, task composition via multitask training in transcribe-translate ratios, and two-stage speech-to-singing adaptation. We also curate a segment-level aligned singing dataset based on the Greek Audio Dataset (GAD) using source separation and CTC forced alignment. Results show that scaling consistently improves performance, while multitask learning acts as a beneficial regularizer primarily for smaller-capacity models. The 2-stage adaptation in Whisper Large-v3 achieves a Word Error Rate (WER) of 27.2%, a significant improvement over zero-shot baselines, establishing the first Greek ALT benchmark.

title: Phases in a class of associative memories via hidden neurons
abstract: Associative memory in the Hopfield network is attractor dynamics in a disordered many-body system, and higher-order and exponential extensions turn its retrieval update into softmax attention. The polynomial and exponential regimes have been analyzed by different methods, with no common architecture in which to ask what fixes the storage scale. In this paper we study the bipartite architecture of Krotov and Hopfield, which we call the class $H$, whose model is fixed by a Lagrangian for each layer, taking the hidden neurons as the order parameter of retrieval. At polynomial load the replica method yields the replica-symmetric phase diagrams and closed-form capacities, and the crosstalk moment is common to Ising and spherical visible neurons, so their differences come from the visible entropy. With a softmax hidden layer the load is exponential, and a copy representation maps the thermodynamics onto random-energy-model counting, with paramagnetic, condensed, and frozen phases. Heating destabilizes retrieval by quantized reassignments of attention, and typical Gaussian patterns remain metastable at every load. The regimes differ in their crosstalk statistics, central-limit at polynomial load and large-deviation at exponential load, and the class $H$ splits retrieval into two roles, the visible Lagrangian fixing stability and the hidden one the storage scale, two axes that may also guide the design of new Lagrangians.

title: Agent systems and applications
abstract: As the number of deployed multi-agent applications increases, further and better experience with the technology is gained, enabling a strong evaluation of the held from a more practical perspective. In particular, questions relating to how the theory of multi-agent systems impacts on practice, and how the practical development itself compares with other technologies, can be answered in the light of a heightened level of maturity. Given the tensions between theoreticians and practitioners in computing in general, let alone their spats in AI or multi-agent systems in particular, the discussion on agent systems and applications was both vigorous and enthusiastic.

title: Dijital Danışmanlık ve Yeni İletişim Arkadaşı Olarak Yapay Zeka
abstract: Yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin gündelik iletişim süreçlerine giderek daha fazla entegre olması, insan–makine etkileşiminin niteliğini dönüştürerek yapay zekânın yalnızca teknik bir araç değil, dijital danışman, karar destek mekanizması ve iletişim partneri olarak konumlanmasına zemin hazırlamaktadır. Bu çalışma, yapay zekânın yeni bir iletişim öznesi ve danışmanlık aktörü olarak ortaya çıkışını iletişimsel, psikolojik ve toplumsal boyutlarıyla ele almaktadır. Yapay zekâ ile kullanıcı arasındaki etkileşim; Sosyal Varlık Kuramı, Sosyal Nüfuz Teorisi ve Sosyal Değişim Teorisi çerçevesinde değerlendirilerek sosyal varlık algısının, kendini açmanın ve etkileşimin sürekliliğinin nasıl oluştuğu tartışılmaktadır. Çalışma, yapay zekânın erişilebilirlik, kişiselleştirme, hızlı geri bildirim ve yargılayıcı olmayan etkileşim özelliklerinin kullanıcıların sisteme yönelik yakınlık ve güven geliştirmesinde belirleyici olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır. Bununla birlikte yapay empati, mahremiyet, veri güvenliği, yanlış yönlendirme, duygusal manipülasyon ve sorumluluk gibi etik sorunlara dikkat çekilmektedir. Sonuç olarak yapay zekâ, insan ilişkilerinin doğrudan ikamesi değil, iletişim biçimlerini yeniden yapılandıran hibrit bir toplumsal aktör olarak değerlendirilmelidir.

Çalışma, yapay zekânın erişilebilirlik, kişiselleştirme, hızlı geri bildirim ve yargılayıcı olmayan etkileşim özelliklerinin kullanıcıların sisteme yönelik yakınlık ve güven geliştirmesinde belirleyici olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır. Bununla birlikte yapay empati, mahremiyet, veri güvenliği, yanlış yönlendirme, duygusal manipülasyon ve sorumluluk gibi etik sorunlara dikkat çekilmektedir. Sonuç olarak yapay zekâ, insan ilişkilerinin doğrudan ikamesi değil, iletişim biçimlerini yeniden yapılandıran hibrit bir toplumsal aktör olarak değerlendirilmelidir.

title: Spectral Rank Bottleneck Dynamics and Low-Rank Adaptation Mechanics Across Sub-Billion Transformer Layers
abstract: This empirical evaluation establishes an extensive diagnostic framework and tensor-level computational audit of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) mechanics across sub-billion parameter transformer models, specifically focusing on the SmolLM2 architecture family (135M to 1.7B parameter baselines). Rather than treating adapter rank scaling as a black-box hyperparameter optimization heuristic, this codebase isolates the mathematical, structural, and runtime dynamics governing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) updates. By projecting weight updates onto decomposed low-rank matrices (ΔW = B · A, where A ∈ ℝ^(r × k) and B ∈ ℝ^(d × r) with rank r ≪ min(d, k)), this repository examines how intrinsic dimensionality bounds govern representation capacity, optimization stability, and hardware execution efficiency. The studies provides various modular, reproducible analysis and interactive diagnostic notebooks designed for layer-wise tensor inspection, spectral auditing, and memory profiling. Core methodological and architectural investigations include: Rank Bottleneck Dynamics & SVD Spectral Profiling: Evaluates singular value decay rates, Frobenius norm retention, and intrinsic rank dimensionality across adapter bottleneck configurations (r ∈ {4, 8, 16, 32}). It quantifies how singular value spectrum energy decays across layers and correlates target rank choices with baseline parameter scale transitions from 135M up to 1.7B parameters (unit5_scaleout_spectra.ipynb). Alpha Scaling Factor (α/r) & Gradient Stability: Analyzes the numerical dynamics of the scaling hyperparameter α/r under varying rank configurations. The suite audits how invariant scaling schedules influence gradient norm trajectories, learning rate dynamics, and matrix delta magnitudes across deep linear projections, preventing optimization collapse during low-rank backpropagation. Target Sub-Layer & Projection Isolation: Diagnoses the differential impact of rank allocation across distinct functional sub-layers of the transformer block. It isolates performance and representation trade-offs when restricting low-rank updates strictly to Multi-Head Attention query/value projections (W_q, W_v) versus Feed-Forward Network expansion gates (SwiGLU W_gate and W_up projection layers). VRAM Allocation & Backpropagation Memory Footprint: Executes detailed CUDA memory profiling to measure exact operational savings during backward passes. It quantifies VRAM footprint reductions achieved by keeping base checkpoint weights W_0 ∈ ℝ^(d × k) strictly frozen while allocating optimizer states (e.g., Adam m and v vectors) exclusively to the low-rank bottleneck parameters A and B. Zero-Latency Weight Merging & Floating-Point Precision Dynamics: Evaluates floating-point accumulation behaviors (FP16, BF16, and FP32) during static adapter weight integration (W_eff = W_0 + (α/r)(B · A)). It quantifies numerical drift and precision degradation during static checkpoint merging, validating zero-latency inference serving without runtime adapter compute overhead.

title: Reproducibility package for: Automatic sign-structure routing of spin Hamiltonians between probabilistic and quantum computing for ground-state energy estimation
abstract: Processed sMTJ measurement data, canonical analysis outputs, per-figure source data and the complete analysis-pipeline code snapshot (code/, MIT license) for the manuscript. The record covers the sMTJ device characterisation (processed per-bias occupancy records, resistance-level estimates, RTN dwell-time records; the 31 GB raw oscilloscope waveforms are not included for size), the sMTJ-calibrated p-bit Gibbs sampler and its Xilinx Kria KR260 FPGA deployment, the sign-structure routing of the 25-model spin-Hamiltonian workload, the executed two-platform hybrid on gauge-incurable instances (IBM Heron ibm_fez / ibm_marrakesh quantum stage with raw bitstring counts and job ids, KR260 probabilistic stage), the matched classical baselines (exact diagonalisation, DMRG, PT2), the size-independent trial-state study, and results/executable_path/recentring_numbers.json, which lists every quantity quoted in the manuscript with its source file. Funding: National Research Council of Science & Technology (NST) grant by the Korea government (MSIT) (No. GTL24043-000); KIST institutional program (26E0031).

title: Recommendations for Implementing Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Nuclear Power Plant Construction Processes
abstract: The report presents application areas for artificial intelligence technologies in nuclear power plant construction based on two complementary models developed by the author: a formal NPP life-cycle model for artificial intelligence and machine learning applications (2025), and a probabilistic optimization and forecasting model for NPP construction projects (2018). For each application area, the report describes the task, the underlying problem, the proposed solution, and examples of model-based implementation. The models can be applied during both the preparatory and main construction phases. Implementation is recommended to begin at the project decision-making stage and continue through commissioning. The NPP life-cycle model may subsequently also be used during operation; however, operational applications are outside the scope of this report. The application areas partially overlap. The same NPP construction task may be considered from the perspective of schedule, supply, requirements, risk, readiness, contracts, or the transition to commissioning. The sections therefore represent different application perspectives within the same integrated modeling framework. The identified application areas define the potential scope for applying the models and artificial intelligence technologies to NPP construction following an initial screening of possible applications. They do not constitute a final implementation portfolio and do not replace subsequent prioritization.

title: Natural Language Processing for Market Sentiment Analysis
abstract: As digital platforms have generated the influx of an increasing amount of unstructured textual data, this has led to a dramatic change in financial market analysis practice and investment decision-making. Natural Language Processing (NLP) is one of the most effective artificial intelligence methods for deriving valuable insights from various information sources, including social media posts, news articles, online forums and communication on the dark web. The chapter examines and vividly illustrates how the tools and tools of NLP can be used to analyze the market sentiment by combining textual information from traditional digital and conventional sources in order to discover patterns of the market, investor actions and financial risks.

title: CEFERA: An Interference and Energy-Aware Federated Analytics Framework for B5G Networks
abstract: The evolution of Beyond 5G (B5G) networks has accelerated the growth of Internet of Things (IoT)-driven smart cities, establishing Federated Analytics (FA) as a vital paradigm for privacy-preserving decentralized data analysis. However, simultaneous multi-user uplink transmissions generate severe residual intra cell interference between users and uncoordinated power consumption, corrupting local updates and delaying analytical convergence. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CEFERA, an interference and energy-aware FA framework. By introducing cross-layer network optimizations for dynamic, non-ideal environments, CEFERA monitors localized channel degradation to prevent uncoordinated power escalation while applying a dynamic power damping strategy to preserve the finite battery reserves of edge devices. Simulation results validate that CEFERA reduces energy consumption by 57.07% and improves the Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) by over 137% compared to the Isolated Power Control (IPC) baseline. This physical-layer stabilization directly translates into superior global analytics, achieving accuracy, precision, and recall metrics above 81%.

title: Quantum Kernel Regression and Variational Quantum Regression for the CCS Prediction of Dissolved Organic Matter: A Comparative Benchmarking Study
abstract: Abstract Recent advances in quantum machine learning (QML) offer new opportunities for chemical property prediction, yet their practical performance relative to established classical models remains poorly characterized on real-world datasets. Building on our previous benchmark of classical and deep learning models for collision cross-section (CCS) predictions, we present an empirical comparison of quantum kernel regression (QKR) and a variational quantum regressor (VQR) against classical machine learning (CML) techniques, including Random Forest (RF), support vector regression (SVR), Lasso, and a Voting Regressor (VR) ensemble. Using an aquatic dissolved organic matter (DOM) dataset with five molecular descriptors and five chemical classes, we systematically investigate QKR feature map repetitions and classical readout kernels, as well as VQR circuit depths and optimizer choices, to identify performance-optimal QML configurations. Regression performance is evaluated using the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R2) across training-set sizes up to 600 molecules per class. Overall, RF and Lasso deliver the most robust CCS predictions, achieving R2 ≥ 0.9 for lignins, carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins. Meanwhile, the optimized QKR architecture exhibits substantial gains as data increase and achieves competitive performance on chemically homogeneous subsets such as carbohydrates and lipids. In contrast, the VQR ansatz remains consistently weaker than both QKR and the classical baselines across all classes and data sizes. The results highlight the strong influence of dataset size, feature representation, and molecular heterogeneity on QML performance while also identifying conditions under which quantum methods may become competitive in future studies.

title: Inverting Self-Triggered Control: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Sparse Denial-of-Service Attacks
abstract: Self-triggered reinforcement learning control (RL-STC) learns the sparsest control schedule that preserves Lyapunov-decreasing stability under a Run-Time Assurance (RTA) override. We invert this: an adversarial RL agent learns the sparsest jamming or Denial-of-Service (DoS) schedule that destabilizes the closed loop, with a Lyapunov-increase admissibility predicate mirroring the defender's safety certificate. We prove a plant-property lower bound on the minimum jam count required for an immediate hold-last medium-access-control adversary to force a crash against a self-triggered controller (STC) satisfying a Lyapunov contract, and recover a certificate-level analog of the consecutive-grouping optimality of prior count-budget DoS scheduling as a corollary. This extends the DoS-scheduling count-budget analysis from periodic and linear-time-invariant to STC controllers. Empirically, we train against four fixed defenders per plant (one Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and three RL-STC) on Pendulum, CartPole, and Quadrotor2D. The learned adversary is the only adversary that crashes every defender on every plant at $100\%$: greedy misses Quadrotor2D LQR on $42\%$ of episodes and periodic misses Pendulum LQR on $97\%$. On jam-time-per-failure it beats baselines by up to $2.8\times$, and shows its widest absolute margin on Quadrotor2D LQR. Robustness ablations show that Gaussian observation noise exceeding the initial-state magnitude and position-only observation both preserve $100\%$ failure rate and keep the learned adversary strictly ahead of both baselines on jam-time-per-failure.

title: PHAT: PHotonic Accelerator for TFHE
abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables secure computation on encrypted data, making it a promising solution for privacy-preserving applications in the cloud. Among various FHE schemes, FHE over the Torus (TFHE) stands out due to its support for arbitrary operations. However, its high computation and communication overhead, particularly in the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) operations required during bootstrapping, limits its practicality for real-world applications. Conventional electronic accelerators struggle to achieve sufficient throughput due to the limitations of technology scaling and the memory-wall problem. To address these challenges, we propose PHAT, a PHotonic Accelerator for TFHE leveraging Optically-addressed Phase-Change Memory (OPCM). OPCM-based processing-in-memory systems offer high computation and communication throughput, making them well-suited for accelerating FFT operations in TFHE. However, directly mapping FFT to OPCM presents challenges such as high-precision analog computation and the high latency and energy cost of programming OPCM cells. To overcome these challenges, we introduce a novel electro-photonic accelerator architecture optimized for TFHE, featuring OPCM-based FFT units, a twiddle-stationary dataflow tailored for OPCM, and a scheduling mechanism to maximize the utilization of the FFT units. PHAT delivers $2.14\times$--$5.10\times$ speedup across four real-world TFHE workloads against the state-of-the-art ASIC accelerator. Our approach significantly enhances the performance of TFHE applications, paving the way for practical and efficient homomorphic encryption in cloud computing.

title: Replication package for "Affine Encoding for Ising Hardware Fixes the Coupling Matrix and Restricts Optima to Supported Pareto Solutions"
abstract: Code, input data, raw result files and run logs that reproduce every measured number in the article. Delivered as a single self-extracting Python file (replication_package.py, --list to inspect, no arguments to unpack) because submission systems flatten archives; all_results.json holds every result and log in readable form so nothing depends on running anything. Each file is listed with its SHA-256 digest in MANIFEST.txt. Python 3.11; numpy, scipy, pymoo, networkx, minor-embedding results additionally use minorminer 0.2.22 and dwave-networkx 0.8.19. No processor access is required. Code under the MIT License; data and result files under CC BY 4.0.

title: Coupling Intelligence to an Existence
abstract: A thought experiment and experimental protocol asking whether irreversibility, lineage, vulnerability and physical coupling alter strategic behaviour in artificial agents. The proposal synthesises existing work in mortal computation, embodied evolution, homeostasis, biohybrid systems and AI alignment, and compares resettable, irreversible-digital and physically coupled experimental conditions. It claims no new mechanism and no empirical result. Conditions A and B are implementable in simulation today.

title: СТРУКТУРНО-МАТЕМАТИЧНА МОДЕЛЬ РЕКОМЕНДАЦІЙНОЇ СИСТЕМИ ПІДБОРУ ОСВІТНІХ РЕСУРСІВ НА ОСНОВІ ОНТОЛОГІЧНИХ ТА СЕМАНТИЧНИХ ОБМЕЖЕНЬ
abstract: У роботі запропоновано структурно-математичну модель рекомендаційної системи підбору освітніх ресурсів, що ґрунтується на інтеграції метаданих навчальних дисциплін і бібліотечних фондів. Формалізація моделі передбачає представлення елементів освітнього процесу у вигляді множин об’єктів і системи відношень між ними, а також використання комплексної функції релевантності, яка поєднує семантичну подібність текстових описів, онтологічну близькість між класами та контекстні освітні обмеження. Семантична складова реалізується через векторне представлення анотацій і ключових слів із застосуванням методів обробки природної мови. Онтологічна складова забезпечує формалізацію ієрархічної структури предметної області, що охоплює навчальні дисципліни та бібліотечні ресурси. Контекстна складова враховує параметри освітнього процесу, зокрема рівень підготовки та рік навчання. Запропонований підхід дозволяє обмежити простір пошуку релевантними об’єктами, підвищити інтерпретованість результатів рекомендації та забезпечити масштабованість системи в умовах зростання обсягів даних. Отримана модель створює формальну основу для реалізації інтелектуальних рекомендаційних систем у цифровому освітньому середовищі закладу вищої освіти.

title: Enhancing Hate Speech Detection in Text and Emojis Using Transformers for Social Media
abstract: Hate speech is a prevalent issue on digital platforms, making it crucial to implement automated methods for its detection and mitigation. This project presents an efficient solution using BERT-based models for hate speech classification. The dataset is annotated at single-word and sentence levels, and preprocessing methods are applied. Machine learning and deep learning models are evaluated based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. A Flask web interface allows users to input text, which is processed and classified by trained models in real time. Enhanced BERT achieves the highest accuracy of 87% for sentence-level classification and 96.1% for single-word classification.

title: Impact of Client Participation on the Trade-Off Between Performance and Computational Cost in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed training without centralizing data, but the trade-offs among predictive performance, local wall-clock execution time, and estimated energy consumption across different FL optimization algorithms remain insufficiently characterized. This paper presents an empirical analysis of how the join ratio affects these trade-offs in a controlled FL setting. Experiments with FedAvg, FedProx, and SCAFFOLD on FashionMNIST considered five join ratio values and five repetitions per configuration. The results show a clear diminishing-returns pattern: increasing the join ratio leads to higher local wall-clock execution time and estimated energy consumption, while the corresponding gains in best test accuracy become progressively smaller. SCAFFOLD achieved the highest mean best test accuracy across all evaluated join ratio values. At a join ratio of 0.10, it also achieved higher mean best test accuracy than FedAvg and FedProx under full participation while exhibiting substantially lower estimated energy consumption. FedAvg at a join ratio of 0.10 nevertheless yielded the highest estimated energy efficiency. Overall, the findings show that the join ratio is an efficiency-related configuration parameter whose effect depends on the adopted FL optimization algorithm within the evaluated setting.

title: Resilience and Risk in the Postpandemic Era
abstract: The chapter gives a detailed account of the knowledge and integration journey of both quantum computing and machine learning by ending it with quantum machine learning (QML) applications. It starts with some fundamental aspects of quantum computing and using qubits, superposition, entanglement, and quantum gates as the building blocks of quantum information processing. The next segment is dedicated to significant quantum algorithms, their structures, their computational benefits, and the character of problems that are to be solved. The difference between classical and quantum computing reveals some significant dissimilarities in modeling, encoding information, and utilization of information in solving problems/tasks. Machine learning basics are introduced to create a point of convergence during integration including the types of models, training, and performance analytics. Areas of overlap between the quantum and machine learning have been discussed, and the strengths of both computing paradigms have been highlighted through the path that will be taken by hybrid quantum-classical architecture. Quantum kernels and quantum-enhanced neural networks are some examples of simple algorithms and methods in QML and are classifiable based on their design guidelines, efficiency, and potential to become quantum-advantaged. Practical cumbersome factors entail data-encoding approach, hardware limitation, and worry mitigation with disorderly scaling quantum (NISQ [noisy intermediate-scale quantum]) equipment. Other practical uses of an advantage of QML are considered in the chapter as well, namely, quantum chemistry, economy and finance, healthcare, logistic systems, and optimization. The issues of scalability, noise resistance, and the creation of standardized benchmarks are mentioned along with the trends in the emerging research. With this step-by-step reasoning, the chapter has attempted to provide the readers with clear understanding of theoretical groundwork and the real-life application of QML solutions to different areas.

title: WinSyn: An Automated Pipeline for Realistic Enterprise Question-Answering Evaluation
abstract: Enterprise settings provide a challenging environment for question-answering agents, which often rely on Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Deep Research (DR), and related techniques. Much of this challenge comes from the complexity of enterprise data: information is often spread across evolving and potentially conflict- ing emails, chat messages, documents, and other artifacts. Existing benchmarks typically have limited real-world complexity, short-form responses, and unnatural queries, so they often fail to capture the challenges of enterprise settings. In this work, we introduce an automated pipeline for generating synthetic datasets of emails reflecting realistic workplace scenarios, along with long- and short-form questions and gold answers grounded in the data. Our method simulates long-running enterprise projects spanning several months and involving up to 25 interacting employees across multiple roles. The data emphasizes ambiguity, distributed information, and naturally occurring queries. To validate the pipeline, we evaluate few standard agentic baselines on our datasets using the latest frontier models. We find that aggregate scores averaged over all queries remain below 80% for each dataset, indicating significant room for improvement. These findings suggest that more work remains to be done for enterprise deployment and underscore the importance of realistic, high-complexity evaluation data for developing stronger real-world enterprise DR systems.

title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Clinical electroencephalography (EEG) data are valuable for healthcare research and for developing artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision-support systems, but EEG recordings and derived features may contain sensitive patient-specific information. This creates privacy risks when data are reused, analyzed, or shared across clinical and research environments. Conventional anonymization methods are often insufficient for high-dimensional biomedical signals, since removing direct identifiers does not necessarily prevent re-identification, linkage, or inference risks. At the same time, strong privacy protection may distort clinically relevant signal characteristics and reduce data utility. This paper studies subject-level differential privacy for protecting clinical EEG-derived feature representations using Gaussian and Laplace perturbations. The proposed framework considers three deployment scenarios: client-side anonymization, centralized server-side anonymization, and decentralized local training. Following EEG preprocessing and feature extraction, Gaussian and Laplace perturbations are applied to the resulting patient-level EEG feature representations. The Laplace experiments evaluate the implemented noise scales, while the scales required for formal full-vector calibration are derived separately. The effects of both perturbations are assessed using statistical utility measures and a downstream machine-learning-based utility check. The results show that differentially private perturbation can be integrated into EEG processing workflows, but the selected mechanism, privacy parameters, and sensitivity calibration strongly influence data utility. The study highlights the practical privacy-utility trade-off in DP-based EEG feature anonymization and the challenges of preserving downstream utility in small and imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

title: From Queries to Narratives: Cultural Heritage Data Stories for Knowledge Graph Exploration and Quality Assessment
abstract: Cultural-heritage KGs such as the NFDI4Culture-KG contain millions of triples about artworks, music, inscriptions, historical events, and the people and places connected to them. For many users, however, discovering this knowledge can be difficult. While SPARQL can be learned, writing meaningful queries first requires an in-depth understanding of the graph's data model, an investment many domain researchers and practitioners are unwilling to make. Even with existing user interfaces, a starting point and some guidance are usually needed, because the data contained in the graph is highly specialized, heterogeneous, and constantly growing, making it challenging to know what it contains or which questions it can answer. In this paper, we present data stories as a way not only to lower this barrier, but also to turn exploration into data-quality assessment, and thus combine accessible querying with the discovery of issues that remain hidden in aggregate statistics. In this contribution, a data story is understood as a narrative document that integrates explanatory text and images with executable SPARQL queries and their visualized results. It is described how they are authored against the graph and how they serve several purposes: guiding users through an unfamiliar graph, creating reproducible narratives, and surfacing data-quality issues previously hidden in aggregate statistics. The authoring platform LODEON including its Sparnatural and AI-supported authoring assistants is introduced as a proof-of-concept. Within the authoring environment, every claim made about the data can be backed by an explicit query, making these narratives transparent and reproducible. This paper also reflects on lessons learned from hands-on seminars and workshops. Early experience suggests that such data stories make cultural-heritage knowledge graphs more accessible for both exploration and quality assessment.

title: The use of large language models for interpreting big data from the internet of things
abstract: Magistrska naloga obravnava uporabo velikih jezikovnih modelov za analizo podatkov interneta stvari (IoT). IoT sistemi zbirajo velike količine heterogenih senzorskih podatkov, ki jih je brez tehničnega znanja težko interpretirati. V nalogi smo sistematično evalvirali zmogljivost šestih velikih jezikovnih modelov pri pretvorbi naravnojezičnih poizvedb v SQL poizvedbe nad tremi javnimi IoT podatkovnimi zbirkami z uporabo 52 standardiziranih poizvedb in petih metrik (točnost, veljavnost SQL, stopnja napak, latenca in strošek) ter ločenega vizualizacijskega preizkusa. Na podlagi ugotovitev smo razvili pogovorno aplikacijo ChatDB, ki združuje pretvorbo naravnega jezika v SQL, samodejno vizualizacijo in generiranje razlag rezultatov v interaktivnem vmesniku.

title: SOMETIMES SOME IS AS GOOD AS ALL
abstract: The representation of partial order semantics as an equivalence relation on interleaving sequences was shown to extend the expressive power of interleaving semantics. A specification formalism called existential specification is introduced in which a formula is interpreted over equivalence classes of sequences by asserting that some (at least one but not necessarily all) sequences from each equivalence class satisfy a given property. It differs from the more common universal specification, which is interpreted over all sequences in all classes. Its advantage over other formalisms that deal with partial order executions lies in its simplicity: any syntax that is defined over interleaving sequences, e.g., linear temporal logic, can be adopted. It is shown how under an appropriate semantical construction, an exact existential specification of a program (i.e., each property of the program expressed using the same formalism is a consequence of this specification) can be given. Moreover, under such a construction, no information about the program is lost by choosing exact existential specification rather than exact universal specification; it is possible to generalise, by means of a proof system, an exact existential specification into an exact universal specification. Applications of these results to achieving compositional proof rules are shown.

title: Getting It Right Is Not Getting It Right the Same Way: Why the Evaluation of Inference in Language Models Requires Process Measures
abstract: Inference and commonsense reasoning in language models are evaluated almost entirely by whether the model's output matches a gold label. This is an outcome measure, and outcome measures have a structural limitation that better items cannot repair: they cannot distinguish a system that performed an inference from a system that retrieved or matched a pattern which rendered the inference unnecessary, because both routes terminate in the same response. We argue that this limitation explains a persistent pattern in the field, in which benchmark scores rise steeply while the failures those benchmarks were built to detect continue to appear, and we argue that it cannot be resolved by adversarial filtering, contamination auditing, or the inspection of generated reasoning traces, each of which remains a function of the model's output. Research on human reading offers a different class of measurement. Reading time, event-related potentials, and hemodynamic response index the cost of bridging, integration, and world-knowledge retrieval while comprehension unfolds, before and independently of whether the reader ultimately answers correctly. We specify what a process-level comparison between reader and model would require, including matched materials, difficulty matched on word frequency and contextual predictability, and matched item sets in which inference is necessary versus items in which it can be bypassed through a surface cue. We then state the failure modes directly. Predictive alignment between model representations and neural signals is not evidence of shared mechanism, and we treat this as a premise rather than a limitation. We close with implications for reporting practice and with a hypothesis, not a finding, about data efficiency.

title: EAIMS: Enterprise AI Maturity Standard
abstract: EAIMS 1.0.0 — Final Release Notes EAIMS 1.0.0 marks the transition from AI maturity assessment to accountable AI operations. Canonical model 8 dimensions 30 capabilities 5 maturity levels 150 capability-specific anchors 206 normative and cross-cutting requirements 177 SHALL/SHALL_NOT requirements 80 critical SHALL/SHALL_NOT requirements Key additions Human Accountability Boundaries (HAB) and Human Reserved decisions A0–A5 AI autonomy classification Agent Permission Envelopes and delegated-authority constraints Operational Suspension Capability Model/System Sourcing Profiles and External Change Exposure Maturity Debt, Autonomy Debt, Assurance Gap, Risk Drift, Autonomy Drift and Scope Drift diagnostics evidence confidence, validity, event invalidation, counter-evidence and conflict semantics G0–G3 gate families and rule-based escalation capability-specific maturity-anchor eligibility Assessment Quality and multi-assessor disagreement/resolution protocols federated maturity and Pilot-to-Scale governance machine-readable specification, schemas and machine-verification rules Executable release validation The release line was promoted after successful hosted validation on RC1 and successful re-validation after merge to main. The release gate includes: 186 executable tests canonical specification integrity validation CLI and synthetic reference-implementation smoke tests Python wheel build and standalone installed-wheel validation dependency vulnerability audit CycloneDX SBOM generation Docker image build and runtime validation Docker Compose configuration and runtime validation execution of all three synthetic reference implementations runtime evidence artifact capture Compatibility The public Python modules eaims.scoring and eaims.reporting and the established validate, score, and report CLI paths remain available. EAIMS 1.0 adds the structured validate-fixture, assess, and review workflows. Evidence boundary EAIMS 1.0 is field-informed rather than field-validated. It does not claim independent multi-organization empirical validation, accredited certification, regulatory approval, representative benchmarking, empirical inter-rater reliability, or completed external independent review. Formal validation remains part of the research agenda. Version provenance The public release is 1.0.0. title: Soil Geochemical Characterization Associated with Fe–Cu Mineralization (Northeastern Aksaray, Türkiye) Using Geochemical Anomaly Classification and Multivariate Statistical Analyses
abstract: This study investigated the soil geochemistry associated with magnetite-bearing Fe–Cu mineralization in northeastern Aksaray (Türkiye). Reservoir normalization, threshold-based geochemical anomaly classification, and multivariate statistical analyses were combined to evaluate the effects of parent lithology, weathering, and mineralization. Reservoir normalization analysis showed pronounced Cu enrichment, together with high geochemical variability, suggesting an influence beyond lithological inheritance alone. The depletion of relatively mobile components and the variable behavior of S further suggested modification of primary geochemical signatures during weathering. Threshold-based anomaly classification showed that positive Cu and Zn anomalies are closely associated with the known Fe–Cu mineralization zones, whereas Fe2O3, Co, and V anomalies primarily reflect basaltic parent rocks and the positive Zr anomaly reflects felsic lithological influence. The multivariate statistical analyses, including correlation analysis (CA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), and principal component analysis (PCA), revealed coherent geochemical associations corresponding to basaltic parent rocks, felsic lithologies, and mineralization-related element assemblages. PCA resolved three principal components reflecting a mafic–felsic lithological contrast (PC1), the survey-scale compositional variability in the As–Pb–Rb–Zr association (PC2), and a Cu–Zn–S mineralization-related signature (PC3). Overall, the results indicate that soil geochemical patterns reflect the overlapping influences of parent lithology, weathering, and Fe–Cu mineralization, emphasizing the importance of local geological background and lithological variability in geochemical anomaly interpretation.

title: Argument Accrual, ASPIC+ and Bipolar Argumentation Frameworks
abstract: In this paper it is studied to which extent various semantics of bipolar argumentation frameworks are correct abstractions of four types of argument support in a version of the ASPIC+ framework with argument accrual. Both positive and negative cases are identified. A novel positive result is that a correct abstraction for conclusion support is identified.

title: A Conversation-Based Approach to Doxastic and Deontic Inference
abstract: We model how conversation dynamics impact the inferences that agents can draw. To this end, we combine an extension of gossip graphs, communication networks that represent information exchange between agents, with logical argumentation. The distance that information travels in communication is used as a proxy for its quality. This way, an ordering over arguments via the elitist preference relation is generated and used to solve conflicts. It is then shown that this preference-based logical argumentation formalism corresponds to approaches based on preferred subtheories, a well-known framework for defeasible reasoning.

title: Safety-aware Skill Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning in Dynamic Environments
abstract: Skill adaptation frameworks based on reinforcement learning often require restrictive assumptions to maintain stability, such as fixed observations or tightly controlled exploration schedules. In cluttered and dynamic environments, however, unrestricted exploration can lead to unsafe behaviour and unstable learning, particularly when task-relevant observations lie near obstacles or involve moving objects. In this work, we present Dist-GPRL, a distance-aware and safety-guided reinforcement learning framework for structured robot skill adaptation. Building upon Gaussian Process (GP)-based skill parameterisation, our framework sequentially adapts overlapping local windows of sparse trajectory via-points rather than modifying the complete skill at every policy step. Raw policy outputs are correlated through the GP covariance structure, producing temporally coherent trajectory updates while reducing the action-space and credit-assignment difficulties associated with global trajectory adaptation. Safety is incorporated through two complementary forms of guidance. A safe-subspace prior derived from the Hausdorff Approximation Planner (HAP) biases policy exploration toward feasible regions, while dynamically updated distance field clearance and gradient rewards provide local obstacle awareness. A trajectory-kinematics similarity regulariser further preserves the demonstrated velocity and acceleration characteristics during adaptation. We evaluate the framework on two dynamic object-manipulation tasks in simulation and transfer the learned policy to real-world robot execution. Experimental results demonstrate higher task success, lower collision frequency, and more stable learning than the baselines, while preserving the kinematic characteristics of the demonstrated skill.

title: Agent-Integrated Software: Interaction Contracts and Continuous Assurance
abstract: Embedding an intelligent agent in an existing application creates a persistent coordination problem: users can revise goals and manipulate shared objects while delegated execution continues. We argue that dependable integration requires an explicit correspondence between task-level interaction and application behavior. We introduce Agent-Integrated Software (AIS) as a software pattern combining a conventional core, direct interaction, and a built-in agent, and Intent-Level Interaction Abstraction (IIA) as the task semantics through which users inspect and control delegated work. An open transition-system model relates AIS execution to IIA states and events. Interaction contracts constrain this relation through task bindings, role-specific authority, control transitions, and outcome evidence; continuous assurance maintains scoped claims as their dependencies change. A compact disclosure contract and conditional propositions illustrate why local component validity is insufficient and how selected admission invariants can be separated from planning. Contrasting software domains expose the framework's assumptions and limits. This perspective develops a research agenda spanning application abstraction, development support, controlled execution, quality assessment, and human supervision, with the aim of making agent integration a maintainable software engineering discipline.

title: Memory-Supported Synergistic Adaptation for Training-Free Test-Time Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) aims to mitigate distribution shifts by adapting models with unlabeled target data at inference time. While TTA with vision-language models (VLMs) has shown promising results in classification, extending it to medical image segmentation remains challenging. In this setting, the adaptation gains from optimizing on VLM-generated predictions are often outweighed by the degradation to the VLM's strong pretrained features caused by noisy, update-driven learning, resulting in limited and unstable improvements. We therefore propose Memory-Supported Synergistic Adaptation (MSSA), a novel training-free TTA framework for medical image segmentation. Without updating model parameters, MSSA dynamically selects reliable image-text predictions to construct an online memory, uses them as text-guided semantic priors, and couples them with cross-image structural alignment for robust adaptation. Specifically, MSSA consists of (i) a noise-aware memory construction module that filters and stabilizes cross-modal predictions, and (ii) a relevance-driven prototype alignment module that aligns the target sample with structurally consistent memory samples and their reliable predictions to improve adaptation. Extensive experiments on multiple medical segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that MSSA consistently improves VLM-based segmentation models and outperforms existing fine-tuning-based TTA methods by a clear margin , with gains of up to 12.2% DSC and 11.7% mIoU. Project Page: https://lingrayy.github.io/MSSA/.

title: A tool for review and comparison of text similarity metrics
abstract: Primerjava podobnosti besedil je pomembna tehnika številnih sodobnih sistemov od spletnih iskalnikov, priporočilnih sistemov do tehnologij RAG, kjer se v fazi pridobivanja (angl. retrieval) prav mera podonosti besedil uporablja za izbiro najustreznejših dokumentov glede na poizvedbo uporabnika. Kljub razširjenosti teh pristopov ni bilo mogoče najti obstoječe rešitve oz. orodja, ki bi uporabniku omogočala na podlagi izbire ene izmed množic vektorskih modelov neposredno primerjavo dveh besedil ali celotnega korpusa besedil, kar je bila motivacija za razvoj rešitve v okviru diplomskega dela. Razvili smo spletno aplikacijo v knjižnici React in ogrodju Flask, ki uporabniku omogoča vnos dveh besedil, izbiro vektorskega modela ter dodatne možnosti preobdelave besedila, kot so občutljivost na velike/male črke, odstranjevanje ločil ter simulacija tipkarskih napak, šuma in premešanih besed. Aplikacija na izbrane metrike izračuna podobnost, poleg tega pa z metodami PCA, t-SNE in UMAP omogoča tudi vizualni prikaz vektorskega prostora besed. V ločenem zavihku je uporabniku predstavljen korpusni način, kjer vnese korpus besedil, izbere vektorski model in poizvedbo, aplikacija pa kot demonstracijo postopka RAG rangira besedila, ki poizvedbi najbolje ustreza.

title: Sistem Pakar Diagnosis Kanker Prostat Berbasis Web Menggunakan Logika Fuzzy Tsukamoto
abstract: Prostate cancer is one of the malignancies most commonly affecting men, particularly older adults, and remains a major contributor to cancer morbidity and mortality worldwide. Diagnosing prostate cancer requires interpreting multiple clinical parameters that are often uncertain and gradual in nature, which complicates medical decision-making. This study aims to design and implement a web-based expert system for prostate cancer risk diagnosis using the Tsukamoto fuzzy logic method. The system was developed with the Laravel 10 framework, PHP 8.1, and a MySQL 8.0 database, using four clinical input variables: Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) level, patient age, International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), and PSA density. A knowledge base of 25 fuzzy rules was formulated through iterative interviews with urology specialists and validated against 50 electronic medical record cases from a referral hospital covering the 2021–2024 period. The inference process follows the Tsukamoto method through fuzzification, rule evaluation using the minimum operator, and weighted-average defuzzification, producing a risk percentage classified into low, medium, or high categories. Black-box testing of eight functional scenarios achieved a 100% success rate. Accuracy testing on 30 of these 50 cases, validated by a urology specialist, yielded an overall accuracy of 90%, with 27 of 30 cases correctly classified. These results indicate that the developed expert system can effectively support early screening of prostate cancer risk and serve as a decision-support tool for healthcare providers, particularly in facilities with limited access to urology specialists.

title: AI Contexts That Never Forget - How to give an artificial intelligence a world it keeps
abstract: A frontier model writes working code and solves competition mathematics. Ask the same model to reconcile three hundred invoices and it loses track of which ones it already processed. A spreadsheet has done that task perfectly since 1985. This article locates the difference, measures it, and names the one operation that closes it. Four reasons this is worth your time. The failure is everywhere and the cause was unnamed. Duplicate actions, stale numbers, a plan built on a fact that changed an hour ago — the industry treats these as separate bugs. They are one mechanism, and this article names it. The field is working on the wrong variable. Almost every 2025–2026 remedy is organised around context length — compress, summarise, evict, fold. This article shows, with the length effect switched off entirely, that length is a bystander. Version multiplicity is the variable. The fix is small, cheap, and measurable. Three operations. The first buys 92% of the available gain and costs less than the baseline it beats. Two standard rebuttals are already dead in the literature. A stronger model leaves the gap open — accuracy falls 92% to 77% on a frontier model, and the gap persists across scale. More memory yields zero recovery: 28% → 28% as memory grows proportionally. The design was specified in 1979 and set aside for tractability. Doyle’s truth maintenance system tracked why each held claim stands, so retracting a premise recomputed what depended on it. Both objections that retired it are engineering, and both are cheaper now. It can be wrong, and it says how. Six tests were committed before any run. Five ran. One refuted the author’s own explanation of the mechanism. The last step is the largest. Repairing the record drives superseded reads to zero and leaves task success flat. Carrying the retirement one step further — into the policy derived from the fact — moves success from 0.782 to 1.000. What this article is. A short, measured account of one mechanism. The experiment is small, the environment is synthetic, and every number is reproducible from the released code. Zero language models were run: that limit is stated here and again at the end. What it uses. The Architecture of Freedom Intelligence — a framework that asks what a system holds as possible before asking what will happen. Section 4 presents it, defends it against its strongest objections, and marks where its own tests located the boundaries.

title: Semantic Artifact Framework: From Documents to Semantic Artifacts
abstract: The Semantic Artifact Framework proposes a knowledge-first form for human, agentic and mixed work. Instead of treating a document, report, paper or README as the primary knowledge container, a represented work maintains a governed Semantic Artifact containing connected knowledge, evidence, questions, decisions, alternatives, attempts, failures, interpretations, provenance and non-erasing history. Documents and interfaces become purpose- and context-specific projections; code, designs, actions and other consequential outputs become traceable derivatives. This release is both the proposal’s canonical semantic form and its self-demonstrating instance. It remains an early research proposal with structurally tested implementation mechanics, not a validated or adopted standard.

title: Tools for decision-level auditing of automated support policies in staged classroom tasks
abstract: Software for auditing what an automated support agent decides, one decision at a time, in a staged classroom task. An agent may be called adaptive on two separate grounds. It may adjust the amount of help it gives to the state of a learner's work, and it may reduce that help as the learner progresses. These are different properties, and a single adaptivity score hides the difference. This package estimates them separately, with cluster resampling and exact intervals appropriate to the small number of clusters a classroom yields, and with a first-order transition model over consecutive decisions. The deposit contains source code, configuration, an environment specification, a synthetic demonstration corpus and run provenance. Run provenance means a column map recording which fields the analysis was permitted to read, cryptographic digests fixing the analysed record set, and a manifest naming the code state, interpreter, package versions, seed and parameters of a run. It contains no records, no derived data, no estimates, no tables and no figures. Record-level data are held under restricted custody and are not released. The digests allow a reader to confirm that a later run examined the same records without any record leaving that custody.

title: ОНТОЛОГІЧНЕ МОДЕЛЮВАННЯ БАЗИ ЗНАНЬ СИСТЕМИ УПРАВЛІННЯ СТАНОМ ЗАМКНУТОГО ВОДНОГО СЕРЕДОВИЩА
abstract: В роботі наведено результати дослідження онтологічного моделювання бази знань системи управління станом водного середовища. У межах дослідження запропоновано модель, що описує процес управління замкнутим водним середовищем. Розроблений підхід передбачає формалізацію предметної області на основі онтологічного моделювання із визначенням ключових сутностей, їх властивостей та взаємозв’язків. Розглянуто інтеграцію даних, отриманих із сенсорів та модулів аналізу зображень, у єдину семантичну структуру. Запропонована модель сприяє підвищенню ефективності моніторингу та керування параметрами водного середовища завдяки семантичній обробці даних і можливості інтелектуального аналізу.

title: A Hybrid Bi-LSTM–CNN Framework for Sentiment Classification of E-Commerce Reviews
abstract: Aspect-Level Sentiment Analysis is a prime example of necessity in an environment like e-commerce, where the primary source of information is reviews that voice the opinion of a feature specifically - be it price, durability or service. In contrast to document-level methods, ALSA yields very fine-grained insights which can be used for making data-driven decisions. Conventional lexicon-based and statistical methods have difficulty with sarcastic expressions, domain terms, complex syntaxes, and implicit aspects. On the other hand, deep learning models like Bi-LSTM, CNNs, and Transformers can eliminate these issues as they are capable of capturing contextual and semantic dependencies. Moreover, attention mechanisms can be used to enhance the interpretability even further. The current study puts forward a hybrid model which integrates Bi-LSTM, CNN, and hierarchical attention for aspect alignment. The results of the experiments on benchmark and Amazon datasets with BERT embeddings indicate a considerable performance enhancement in comparison with baselines.

title: A Hybrid Quantum-Heuristic Feature Selection Approach Using Grover's Algorithm, PSO and ACO
abstract: A new hybrid feature selection method, combining Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimisation (ACO) techniques, is proposed to improve classification performance and reduce computational costs, particularly in high-dimensional data. The approach is tested on Breast Cancer and Madelon datasets, showing superior results. The method’s embedding of classical metaheuristics in a quantum-inspired search framework increases exploration-exploitation trade-off, making it more effective. The approach is planned for further expansion to larger datasets.

title: Pharma of the World to Pharma Powerhouse of the World
abstract: India's ambition to move from “pharmacy of the world” to a genuine “pharma powerhouse” hinges on whether its startups can turn artificial intelligence (AI) from a buzzword into a measurable growth engine. This study asks a direct question: when Indian pharma and health technology startups adopt AI, does it actually translate into stronger performance, faster innovation, and greater investment readiness—and under what organizational conditions does this happen? Focusing on Bengaluru's pharma–health technology ecosystem, we surveyed 142 managerial-level professionals using a 19-item scale that captures perceived benefits, financial effects, innovation outcomes, and team-level enablers of AI adoption. Reliability and validity were established through Cronbach α (0.878), Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin (0.862), and exploratory factor analysis, which revealed four underlying dimensions: (1) AI adoption and operational integration, (2) AI-driven innovation and time-to-market, (3) financial impact and investment readiness, and (4) team diversity and cross-functional collaboration. These components were then modeled using ordinal logistic regression to test five hypotheses linking AI-related capabilities to perceived startup growth and performance. The final model showed excellent fit and strong explanatory power, indicating that higher AI adoption, stronger innovation pipelines, robust AI-aligned financial planning, and supportive, diverse teams are all significantly associated with higher perceived performance levels. Multiple-response analysis adds texture to these findings. Respondents most frequently reported using AI in financial forecasting and investment analysis, drug discovery and molecule design, regulatory compliance, and customer engagement, while simultaneously struggling with integration into legacy processes, talent shortages, ethical and regulatory uncertainty, and data quality gaps. In this sense, the work aligns closely with the broader lens of engineering thermodynamics and recovery management : AI-enabled startups are treated as sociotechnical systems that must minimize “waste” in the form of idle capacity, rework, and underused data, while maximizing recovery of value from R&D, capital, and knowledge flows. By viewing AI as a mechanism for improving systemic efficiency and recovery—rather than as a stand-alone digital add-on—the study offers a nuanced view: AI is already acting as a multidimensional enabler for Indian pharma startups, but its full potential will only be realized when technological investments are matched by organizational readiness, capability-building, and thoughtful change management.

title: A System for Anonymous Age Verification Using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
abstract: Digitalne storitve za dostop do vsebin, neprimernih za mladoletne osebe, vse pogosteje zahtevajo preverjanje starosti uporabnikov. Obstoječe rešitve, kot so samoizjave, biometrično ocenjevanje in nalaganje slik osebnih dokumentov, so bodisi trivialno zaobidljive bodisi izpostavljajo uporabnike tveganju zlorabe osebnih podatkov. V diplomskem delu smo zato zasnovali in implementirali sistem za anonimno preverjanje starosti, ki temelji na dokazih brez razkritja (zk-SNARK, sistem Groth16). Sistem sestoji iz izdajatelja preverljivih poverilnic, denarnice v obliki razširitve za brskalnik Firefox in preverljivca v obliki spletne strani. Za zgoščevanje podatkov in podpisovanje smo uporabili kriptografske gradnike, prilagojene za delo znotraj vezij Circom (funkcijo Poseidon in krivuljo Baby JubJub). Naše vezje AgeCheckV2 vsebuje 4480 omejitev, generacija dokaza v povprečju traja 418 ms, njegovo preverjanje pa 1022 ms. Analiza je pokazala, da preverljivec iz dokaza ne more razbrati ničesar razen izpolnjenosti pogoja, kar sistem loči od obstoječih pristopov, kot je selektivno razkrivanje. Sistem trenutno ne rešuje preklica poverilnic in temelji na simulirani zaupanja vredni namestitvi, kar sta glavni oviri pred morebitno produkcijsko uporabo.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Educational Assessment under Item-Calibration Uncertainty
abstract: Adaptive educational assessment must make sequential item-selection decisions while both learner proficiency and item parameters are uncertain. Conventional maximum-information rules typically treat calibrated item difficulty as fixed, whereas reinforcement-learning policies often encode uncertainty only implicitly in a latent state. This paper proposes UA-DoubleQ, an uncertainty-aware reinforcement-learning framework that exposes posterior learner uncertainty and item-calibration uncertainty directly to the decision process. A Bayesian ability belief is maintained on a discretized latent-proficiency grid. At each step, a Double Q-learning controller selects a risk coefficient that modulates a robust Fisher-information score; the same controller can terminate the assessment when continued measurement is not worth its cost. This design separates uncertainty estimation from risk scheduling and allows the policy to become more conservative when item-parameter uncertainty is consequential. We evaluate the method in an ASSISTments-calibrated semi-synthetic benchmark, required because historical logs do not provide counterfactual responses to unadministered items. Across three independent seeds with 500 test examinees per seed, UA-DoubleQ used 14.02±1.25 questions, achieved ability RMSE 0.444±0.042, 92.1±1.1% empirical 95% interval coverage, and selected items with mean difficulty standard error 0.237. Relative to a vanilla Double-Q policy without uncertainty in the state, UA-DoubleQ shortened assessments by 17.0%, improved coverage by 1.8 percentage points, and reduced selected-item calibration uncertainty by 4.8%, with an explicitly quantified RMSE trade-off. Relative to point-estimate maximum Fisher information, it reduced RMSE by 14.9% and improved coverage by 4.3 percentage points. The results support uncertainty-conditioned risk scheduling as a practical middle ground between aggressive information maximization and conservative uncertainty-aware selection.

title: The Dead-Drop Family: Information-Theoretic Asynchronous Messaging Over Substrates You Do Not Own
abstract: Every deployed asynchronous messenger concedes something to the party holding the message while the recipient is offline. It concedes content to a computational cipher the operator may one day break or be compelled to break; or it concedes availability to an operator who must remain willing to serve; or both. We describe a family of constructions that concede neither, by making the storage layer irrelevant rather than trustworthy. A message is sealed under pre-shared one-time-pad material with a Wegman–Carter one-time authenticator, tagged with a pad-derived identifier that both endpoints compute independently and that no third party can predict or link, and then deposited on any substrate that will hold bytes and return them when asked. The recipient, whenever they next come online, derives the identifiers they expect and retrieves whatever is waiting. The doctrine this family rests on is a single sentence: when content is information-theoretically sealed, the storage layer is fungible. We state it once and then instantiate it three times, on substrates chosen because they differ on every axis that matters — retention, cost, bandwidth, permanence, and what the operator can be compelled to do. Substrate A is a federation of public relays, giving high bandwidth and days-to-weeks retention at the cost of depending on operators who may vanish. Substrate B is the Bitcoin blockchain via OP_RETURN, giving permanence and proof-of-work anchoring at the cost of transaction fees and a wallet. Substrate C is the network of public timestamping calendars, giving permanence with no wallet and no funds at the cost of a bandwidth ceiling so severe that the channel carries a selection among codebook entries rather than content. We give the shared construction once, a single threat model with per-substrate deltas, one comparison, and an honest account of what each substrate costs. We are explicit throughout about what this family does not provide: it protects content unconditionally and metadata hardly at all, and on that second axis the deployed alternatives are frequently better. Keywords: dead drop, store-and-forward, one-time pad, information-theoretic security, asynchronous messaging, substrate independence, metadata, Bitcoin, timestamping, relay federation. ---

title: RetainQAudit: Paired retain-q selection-change auditing for ragged rating arrays
abstract: RetainQAudit is a bounded Python package for auditing selection changes under a per-item retain-q constraint in ragged rating arrays. It constructs unconstrained and capacity-constrained removal sets from the same priority order, exports exchanged members, verifies target-coverage accounting, and retains explicit failure states. Users supply the target labels and protocol; the software does not infer ground truth or prescribe which observations to remove. This software-only archive contains the frozen version 0.1.0 wheel and source distribution, a six-row artificial example, deterministic expected example outputs, and a bounded core test suite. It excludes the study's real data, manuscript, full-array results and institutional documents. Local checks use CPython 3.12.10 and NumPy 2.4.3 on macOS arm64; 243 included tests passed. These are same-team software checks, not external reproduction, user evaluation, clinical validation or full-paper reproduction. Archive revision: 20260910-r1.

title: MetaPCR-LLM: Universal Proof-Carrying Reasoning Across Heterogeneous Logics for Large Language Model Validation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly produce reasoning that combines deductive, abductive, probabilistic, defeasible, temporal and constraint-based inference, yet most symbolic validation approaches assume a single target logic or translate heterogeneous reasoning into one common formalism. We introduce MetaPCR-LLM, a proof-carrying framework for validating LLM reasoning across heterogeneous native logics. MetaPCR-LLM represents a reasoning trace as a typed proof graph in which each step is assigned to an appropriate native validator and carries a proof certificate or machine-checkable witness together with provenance, uncertainty, temporal, and defeasibility metadata. Transitions between logical systems are treated as explicit proof-carrying bridges, allowing the framework to distinguish locally valid inference from globally invalid cross-logic composition. Counter-abduction further tests accepted explanations against independently validated alternatives, while the same mechanism supports certified recomposition of reasoning fragments produced by multiple LLMs. We evaluate the framework on Truthful-Halluc, Med-Halluc, eSNLI-Halluc and Autoimmune-narrate-halluc across single- and mixed-logic reasoning regimes. MetaPCR-LLM achieves 0.86 overall accuracy, 0.88 step-validity accuracy and 0.86 chain-certification accuracy, with a cross-dataset macro-F1 of 0.838. Its pooled hallucination F1 reaches 0.83, compared with 0.77 for the ValidLLP-style baseline, an absolute improvement of 0.06 at the reported precision. The advantage remains especially pronounced on heterogeneous reasoning: mixed-logic F1 reaches 0.80, compared with 0.74 for ValidLLP-style validation and 0.70 for MetaPCR without bridge checking. Bridge validation reaches 0.88 accuracy and explicit proof diagnostics improve failure-type and validator localization. In multi-LLM recomposition, the complete certificate--bridge--label configuration reaches 0.86 accuracy and reduces invalid compositions from 0.29 to 0.18. Human evaluation further shows an increase in reasoning-assessment accuracy from 0.68 to 0.88. These results show that proof-carrying heterogeneous validation improves the aggregate answer-level comparison while also providing reliable composition, localization and auditing of reasoning that spans multiple formal systems.

MetaPCR-LLM represents a reasoning trace as a typed proof graph in which each step is assigned to an appropriate native validator and carries a proof certificate or machine-checkable witness together with provenance, uncertainty, temporal, and defeasibility metadata. Transitions between logical systems are treated as explicit proof-carrying bridges, allowing the framework to distinguish locally valid inference from globally invalid cross-logic composition. Counter-abduction further tests accepted explanations against independently validated alternatives, while the same mechanism supports certified recomposition of reasoning fragments produced by multiple LLMs. We evaluate the framework on Truthful-Halluc, Med-Halluc, eSNLI-Halluc and Autoimmune-narrate-halluc across single- and mixed-logic reasoning regimes. MetaPCR-LLM achieves 0.86 overall accuracy, 0.88 step-validity accuracy and 0.86 chain-certification accuracy, with a cross-dataset macro-F1 of 0.838. Its pooled hallucination F1 reaches 0.83, compared with 0.77 for the ValidLLP-style baseline, an absolute improvement of 0.06 at the reported precision. The advantage remains especially pronounced on heterogeneous reasoning: mixed-logic F1 reaches 0.80, compared with 0.74 for ValidLLP-style validation and 0.70 for MetaPCR without bridge checking. Bridge validation reaches 0.88 accuracy and explicit proof diagnostics improve failure-type and validator localization. In multi-LLM recomposition, the complete certificate--bridge--label configuration reaches 0.86 accuracy and reduces invalid compositions from 0.29 to 0.18. Human evaluation further shows an increase in reasoning-assessment accuracy from 0.68 to 0.88. These results show that proof-carrying heterogeneous validation improves the aggregate answer-level comparison while also providing reliable composition, localization and auditing of reasoning that spans multiple formal systems.
